title: Suspected Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Faecal Calprotectin and Referral Pathway

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult suspected IBD assessment, stool and blood testing, infection exclusion and urgent referral for severe disease.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national inflammatory bowel disease guideline was identified in the sources opened on 14 October 2026. NICE guidance is an international comparator pending Saudi/local adaptation.
SFDA product registration was not verified; any medicine selection requires the current Saudi Drug Information register and hospital formulary.
The local faecal-calprotectin threshold and two-week referral route require Saudi service confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Immune-mediated mucosal inflammation causes ulceration and bleeding. Crohn's disease may affect any gastrointestinal segment and can be transmural. Ulcerative colitis is continuous colonic mucosal inflammation beginning at the rectum. Inflammation impairs absorption and can cause anaemia, weight loss and extra-intestinal disease.
keyMechanisms: Immune-mediated mucosal inflammation causes ulceration and bleeding.
Crohn's disease may affect any gastrointestinal segment and can be transmural.
Ulcerative colitis is continuous colonic mucosal inflammation beginning at the rectum.
Inflammation impairs absorption and can cause anaemia, weight loss and extra-intestinal disease.

symptoms: Persistent diarrhoea, rectal bleeding, urgency, abdominal pain, nocturnal stooling, weight loss or fatigue.
physicalSigns: Pallor, fever, tachycardia, abdominal tenderness, perianal disease, weight loss or extra-intestinal findings.
redFlags: Haemodynamic instability, severe bleeding, toxic megacolon concern, obstruction, perforation, sepsis or marked dehydration needs emergency admission.
precipitants: Infection can mimic or precipitate a flare; NSAIDs and smoking affect risk or course.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Pathogen or exposure history with acute onset.
No bleeding, weight loss, nocturnal progression or objective inflammation.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Above the locally validated assay threshold
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use the local pathway for repeat testing or gastroenterology referral; it is not a cancer test.
ruleIn.normalValue: Below the locally validated low-risk threshold

clinicalManagement.title: Identify severe or complicated disease
actions: Admit urgently for instability, severe bleeding, systemic toxicity, obstruction, perforation, abscess or severe dehydration.
Assess hydration, weight, abdominal/perianal findings and extra-intestinal symptoms.

clinicalManagement.title: Obtain targeted tests
actions: Request FBC, CRP/ESR, renal/liver profile, coeliac serology, stool pathogens and faecal calprotectin when cancer is not suspected.
Use the urgent suspected-cancer pathway instead when cancer alarm features dominate.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer for diagnostic endoscopy
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Urgency based on severity and local pathway
actions: Refer raised calprotectin or persistent inflammatory features to gastroenterology for ileocolonoscopy and biopsy.
Safety-net normal or borderline results when bleeding, weight loss, nocturnal symptoms or clinical concern persists.

medicationPlan.note: Do not start IBD-specific anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive treatment before diagnostic assessment unless directed by gastroenterology.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Adults with recent-onset lower-GI symptoms when specialist assessment is being considered and cancer is not suspected.

teaching.scope: Adult suspected IBD assessment, stool and blood testing, infection exclusion and urgent referral for severe disease.
learningObjectives: Use calprotectin in the correct population.
Exclude infection and recognise severe disease.
pitfalls: Using calprotectin when cancer is suspected.
Delaying admission in systemic toxicity or obstruction.
keyPoints: Calprotectin indicates inflammation but does not diagnose IBD by itself.
Normal blood inflammatory markers do not exclude bowel-limited disease.

patientEducation: Explain the purpose and limitations of calprotectin and endoscopy.
lifestyleAndDiet: Maintain hydration and nutrition; avoid non-prescribed NSAIDs and smoking.
mdtReferrals: Gastroenterology, endoscopy, radiology and dietetics according to severity.
dischargeCriteria: Stable for outpatient work-up, able to hydrate, no emergency feature and referral/safety-net documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Track results and referral; reassess urgently for heavier bleeding, fever, severe pain, distension, vomiting or dehydration.
